Was the industrial revolution primarily only helpful to the wealthy or is it truly responsible for creating our middle class system in the US?

The Industrial Revolution was a bitch, especially in England. A lot of people really suffered and died during the transition between agrarian and industrial. Poverty reached new lows, workers were exploited, efforts to organize in the United States in the 1870's was bitterly fought by the industrial magnates (a loooooong story in and of itself). However, over time as the economy adapted to industrialization, and as the evils inherent in the abuse of the system (I'm biased towards capitalism, however I believe it, like most other economic isms is subject to abuse by the hands of greedy and selfish people) became more apparent, a rising social movement helped to ease those evils. If we look at the 20th century for examples, we can see the Roaring 20's and the 1950's are seen as halcyon moments of ultimate middle class prosperity, and in each case they were driven by post war manufacturing economies. Trade and commerce has typically driven and created the middle classes, and with the increased trade created by the industrial revolution, it is safe to argue that it did in fact create the broad middle class system in the US. Without widespread industrialization we'd be reduced to local level manufacturing and farming and subsequently fewer opportunities to participate in a middle class economy. Basically, fewer people would have the luxury of time away from seeing to their own sustenance and the greater concentration of capital that drives the middle class.

Tl;Dr. The Industrial Revolution made the middle class, but lots of Bad Things happened during the transition to an industrial society, typical for any sort of revolution and massive social upheaval. We still feel the lingering effects of some of them today. Hug a skilled trades worker (union or not), and buy American.
